description: Instance batch this parametrization applies to. Vehicle parameters attach to the BATCH, not to an individual instance: all instances of a batch share one parametrization. ON DELETE CASCADE.

Vehicle type being parametrized. Join raw_data.vehicles to separate truck rows (vehicle_type = 'Ground') from robot rows (vehicle_type = 'Autonomous'). ON DELETE CASCADE. Not every cataloged vehicle type necessarily carries rows here.
Maximum number of robots carried on the truck. NULL for robot rows and for batches that do not bound the carried fleet.
Number of robots loaded on the truck at the depot. NULL for robot rows.
Maximum number of parcels the vehicle can carry. NULL where parcel capacity is not modeled.
Number of parcels loaded at the depot. NULL where not modeled.

Distance-dependent operating cost. IS in SI: per METRE, not per kilometer, e.g., 0.2 EUR/km is stored as 0.0002. Multiply by 1000 to recover the familiar figure. Combines directly with the distances in m in raw_data.travel_matrices.
Energy price used to cost energy consumption. IS in SI: per JOULE.

Time-dependent cost, typically the driver wage. IS in SI: per SECOND, not per hour, so a wage of 30 EUR/h is stored as 0.008333333333333333. Multiply by 3600 to recover the familiar figure. Combines directly with durations in s.

Penalty cost per unit of delay beyond a customer deadline. IS in SI: per SECOND, not per hour -- 5 EUR/h is stored as 0.001388888888888889. Multiply by 3600 to recover the familiar figure. NULL for batches that do not permit or do not penalize delay.
Conversion from fuel (liter) consumed to CO2-equivalent emissions. Parameter of the emission model. IS in SI: per CUBIC METRE of fuel, not per litre.
Conversion from energy consumed to CO2-equivalent emissions. Parameter of the emission model. IS in SI: per JOULE, not per kWh.
Monetary valuation of emissions, used where the objective internalises emission cost.
Handling/service time per served request at a customer or location to drop off the robots. Distinct from travel and waiting time.
Duration of a single interruption stop, for example a traffic-light or pedestrian-crossing stop for a robot or a truck. NULL where interruptions are not modeled.

Expected number of interruption stops per unit of TRAVEL DISTANCE, for example traffic-light or pedestrian-crossing stops for a robot every 100 meters. Multiply by travel time to obtain the expected number of stops. NULL where interruptions are not modeled.

Minimum travel speed. Where only one speed applies, a batch may record the same value in speed_min and speed_max. Note the unit: 30 km/h is stored as 8.333333333333334 and 5 km/h as 1.3888888888888888.
Maximum travel speed. Potentially NULL where a speed range is not modeled.
Acceleration used in the kinematic component of the energy model.
Deceleration, reported as a POSITIVE magnitude, not as a negative value.
Empty vehicle weight. Together with the payload it forms the total mass in the energy model.
Correction factor accounting for the inertia of rotating drivetrain components.
Maximum payload mass. NULL where weight capacity is not modeled.
Maximum distance per tour. NULL where tour length is unbounded.
Frontal surface area used in the aerodynamic drag term of the energy model.
Fuel-to-air mass ratio. Parameter of the combustion engine model.
Engine friction factor. IS in SI: joules per cubic meter of displacement per revolution, not kJ/(rev*L).
Engine speed, i.e. revolutions per second expressed as a plain reciprocal second. Parameter of the combustion engine model.
Engine displacement. IS in SI: cubic meters, not litres -- a 3 L engine is 0.003 m^3.
Lower heating value of the fuel. IS in SI: joules per kilogram, not kJ/g. Parameter of the combustion engine model.
Fuel density. IS in SI: kilograms per cubic meter, not g/L. Converts between fuel mass and fuel volume in the emission model.
Engine efficiency parameter.
Drivetrain efficiency: share of engine output reaching the wheels.
Share of kinetic energy recovered when braking. 0 for vehicles without regenerative braking.
Share of potential energy recovered when descending. Meaningful only for batches with non-flat topography.
Constant power draw of auxiliary systems such as cooling or electronics, independent of motion. IS in SI: watts, not kW.
Usable battery capacity. IS in SI: joules, not kWh. Infinity denotes a non-binding battery, i.e. energy is not a limiting resource in that batch. Never cast to integer.
Charging power at a charging station. IS in SI: watts, not kW. Infinity denotes instantaneous recharging. Never cast to integer.
Distance-specific energy consumption, used as a simplified alternative where the detailed emission model is not applied. IS in SI: joules per meter, not kWh/m.
Aerodynamic drag coefficient. Used with frontal_area and air_density in the drag term.
Rolling resistance coefficient of the tires on the road surface.
Air density assumed in the aerodynamic drag term.
Gravitational acceleration assumed in the rolling resistance and gradient terms.
